claims.scope: For finite nonempty player and phase types, nonnegative survival coefficients, a strict joint contraction, and the stated cyclic one-step inequalities imply that some player has base value at least eta divided by twice the player cardinality. The theorem is game-independent aggregation infrastructure and consumes its coefficient, contraction, and recurrence hypotheses.

claims.subject: Finite normalized-hazard seam compactness
claims.scope: For a fixed finite player type, nonnegative positive periodic hazards, vanishing normalized signed seams, and a vanishing normalized matrix residual, a subsequence of normalized cumulative hazards converges to a nonnegative simplex kernel. The result is game-independent compactness; it does not produce periodic blocks or game-semantic hypotheses.

claims.subject: Sorin's absorbing-game uniform-payoff segment
claims.scope: Every payoff (a, 2(1-a)) with 1/2 <= a <= 2/3 is realized against all unilateral behavioral deviations; the account strategy may depend on the requested accuracy.

quitting_frontier.summary: The quitting dependency DAG has two open producer arrows: the chronological arrow requires both an actual reached-port packet kernel and an external low-debt candidate adapter. The paid arrow has a full-gap cap port at every literal profile, quantitative excess-debt contraction, and actual ports approaching the inert minimum-fiber boundary; it still needs a consumer or regeneration theorem for quantitative descent, or a consumer for the literal inert stall. Separately, exact Fin4 scale search makes existence of a positive-gap reward recursively enumerable, but produces no positive instance and gives no conclusion on nontermination. The general and all-quitting conjectures remain open independently of any one certificate grammar.
